author: bd-spin/bd-spin-20260513T014512Z-2345176
text:
Empirical finding while planning this bead: PKITS EE certs have NO SAN and NO EKU (verified ValidCertificatePathTest1EE.crt — Subject is C/O/CN only, no AltName or ExtKeyUsage extension). All verify_* wrappers enforce EKU via their Profile (BasicTlsProfile requires id-kp-serverAuth per pkix-profiles/src/lib.rs:206; analogous EKU requirements in BasicSmimeProfile and the code-signing/timestamping profiles). Therefore verify_tls_server / verify_smime_signer / verify_smime_recipient / verify_code_signer / verify_time_stamper applied to a PKITS chain will uniformly reject every chain at the chain-validation step (EKU missing), before any identity binding runs.

The bead description acknowledges PKITS lacks hostname/mailbox SANs and proposes curated corpora for those — but the bigger structural issue is that PKITS does not exercise EKU at all, so "PKITS regression for the NEW per-use wrappers" is infeasible without re-issuing the leaves.

Options:

(A) RESCOPE: drop "PKITS through wrappers" entirely. Bead becomes curated-corpus only (RFC 6125 §6.4 hostnames + RFC 8398 mailboxes + code-signing/timestamping curated cases). PKITS regression for the chain-validation engine stays the responsibility of pkix-chain/tests/e2e.rs (which already covers verify_chain_default against PKITS 4.1.1) plus the existing pkix-difftest pkix_path oracle (which covers the full 247-chain PKITS corpus). This is the AGENTS.md-aligned path: no test-vector derivation, no profile weakening, faithful to the wrappers' design contract.

(B) BUILD PKITS-DERIVED FIXTURES: re-issue selected PKITS leaves with SAN + EKU appropriate to each wrapper. Substantial fixture-generation effort. Requires deciding what hostname/mailbox to attribute to each. Uses an external oracle (pyca/cryptography or openssl) to re-sign, keeping the test-vector chain intact at the cost of inventing identity data. The PKITS chain shape is preserved but the leaves are derived, which is in tension with — though not strictly forbidden by — AGENTS.md "no test vectors from code under test" (the *code under test* is pkix-chain, not the fixture-generation tooling; the leaves would be signed by a NIST CA we own the private key for in the PKITS corpus).

(C) PERMISSIVE TEST PROFILE: introduce a no-EKU profile for testing only. Violates BasicTlsProfile design contract; weakens the test signal; rejected on AGENTS.md test-integrity grounds.

Recommendation: (A). PKITS' value is for the §6.1 chain engine, where it is already exercised in two places. The wrapper-level acceptance criteria are about identity binding and EKU enforcement, which PKITS cannot exercise without fabrication. The curated-corpus deliverable is the substantive work; PKITS-through-wrappers does not add signal commensurate with the fixture-generation cost.

Releasing claim and labeling human for your decision. If (A): suggest closing this bead as superseded and filing two children under PKIX-fmtv covering "Curated RFC 6125 hostname corpus + verify_tls_server tests" and "Curated RFC 8398 mailbox corpus + verify_smime_signer/recipient tests" (the code-signing and timestamping wrappers don't have analogous identity-string targets, so their wrapper acceptance is just "EKU enforced; rejects chain without id-kp-codeSigning / id-kp-timeStamping," which can be a few targeted unit tests rather than a curated corpus).
